categories.main_business_segments: CarMax operates in two primary business segments: CarMax Sales Operations and CarMax Auto Finance (CAF). CarMax Sales Operations encompasses all aspects of auto merchandising and service operations, including retail and wholesale vehicle sales, vehicle purchases, related products and services, and arranging financing. CAF is dedicated solely to providing vehicle financing to customers purchasing retail vehicles from CarMax stores.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: CarMax leverages a proprietary omni-channel platform that integrates cloud-based and in-house technologies, advanced data science, AI, and machine learning to optimize inventory management, pricing, customer experience, and operational efficiency. The company employs Agile, DevOps, and Lean methodologies in software development, and utilizes centralized inventory management and pricing systems, digital appraisal tools, and AI-powered virtual assistants to streamline the car buying and selling process.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CarMax primarily serves individual consumers seeking to buy or sell used vehicles, as well as licensed automotive dealers through its wholesale auctions. The company targets a broad spectrum of retail customers across the credit spectrum and also provides services to dealers via digital appraisal products and auctions. End markets include retail used vehicle buyers, wholesale vehicle dealers, and customers seeking vehicle financing and protection plans.
categories.geographic_coverage: CarMax operates 250 used car stores across 109 U.S. television markets, covering approximately 85% of the U.S. population. Its retail and wholesale operations span 41 states, with significant concentrations in the Southeastern U.S., California, Texas, and the Washington, D.C./Baltimore area. The company also operates stand-alone reconditioning and auction facilities and maintains a nationwide digital presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: CarMax operates primarily at the downstream end of the automotive supply chain, focusing on retailing used vehicles directly to consumers and conducting wholesale auctions for vehicles not meeting retail standards. The company also sources vehicles upstream from consumers, dealers, auctions, and fleet owners, and provides in-house and third-party financing solutions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: CarMax's strategic priorities center on expanding its omni-channel capabilities, leveraging data science and AI to enhance customer and associate experiences, and driving operational efficiencies in logistics and reconditioning. The company is focused on growing its market share, expanding its store and capacity footprint, scaling CAF across the full credit spectrum, and becoming a leading retailer of used electric vehicles. Ongoing investments target digital innovation, customer-centric tools, and partnerships to support long-term growth.
categories.revenue_model: CarMax generates revenue primarily through the sale of used vehicles at retail, wholesale vehicle auctions, and related products and services such as extended protection plans and vehicle repair. Additional revenue streams include financing income from CAF, fees from third-party finance providers, advertising and subscription revenues from Edmunds, and service department operations. The company employs a no-haggle pricing model and offers both in-store and online transaction options.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CarMax faces competition from franchised new and used car dealers, independent used car dealers, online and mobile sales platforms, and private sellers. Major competitors include franchised dealerships with certified pre-owned programs and online-focused retailers. CarMax is the largest used vehicle retailer in the U.S., with an estimated 3.7% market share of 0- to 10-year-old used vehicles, and differentiates itself through its omni-channel platform, customer-centric experience, and scale.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2025, CarMax reported net sales and operating revenues of $26.4 billion, with a gross profit of $2.9 billion and net earnings of $501 million. The company sold 789,050 used vehicles at retail and 544,312 vehicles at wholesale, with a modest 0.8% increase in used vehicle revenues and a 3.1% increase in used unit sales year-over-year. CarMax maintains a strong liquidity position, continues to invest in growth, and targets double-digit EPS growth over the long term.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CarMax emphasizes a unique, customer-centric value proposition built on competitive, no-haggle pricing, a broad selection of quality certified vehicles, and a seamless omni-channel experience that allows customers to buy or sell on their own terms. The company differentiates itself through its transparent sales process, proprietary technology, extensive inventory, and integrated financing options, aiming to deliver the most convenient and trustworthy car buying and selling experience in the industry.
